column1: # scriptvm-dispatch.tsv - the script verb -> native handler mapping, 1,493 rows.
# PROVENANCE IS PER COLUMN. These four columns do not share a source and must not be quoted as
#   call_id      the record index into the dispatch table, stride 0x20.
#   handler      RE-DERIVED FROM THE BINARY 2026-09-08: read at 01EED720 + 0x20*call_id and
#                compared against the prior extraction. 1,224 of 1,224 agree; 0 fall outside
#                HEADER-LINES-STILL-OLD-FRAME. This header said the value is "table[+0x00]". It is
#                not. The table base is 01EED700 (count at +0, record 0 at +8), so 01EED720 is
#                tbl+0x20 and 01EED720 + 0x20*call_id is tbl+32+32*call_id - exactly what
#                VMNativeCommandDispatch_GetResultCallback (003DC2A0) reads, which in the record's
#                own frame is +0x18. EVERY VALUE IN THIS COLUMN STANDS; what was wrong is which
#                callback it is. A reader who took "+0x00" literally would treat a RESULT callback
#                as a BEGIN callback and would never get an async verb to work.
#                THE COLUMN NAME IS STILL `handler` and renaming it to `result_callback` is a
#                schema change with consumers (scriptvm_dispatch_verify.py at least), so it is
#   verb, args   FROM THE AUTHORED ff12-script CATALOG, an external community source of 1,954
#                verb names. NOT verifiable against the image. A name here is a lead.
#                TRANSCRIPTION RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-14 against the bundled source itself
#                1,224 of 1,224 verb names identical by call id, 0 ids absent from the catalog.
#                That settles TRANSCRIPTION, not semantics - the catalog is an authored artifact,
#                so an agreeing name still means "the corpus copied the catalog faithfully" and
#                not "this is what the engine calls that verb". FINAL-AUDIT pass 25.
#   owner        the GFZ ledger's owner tag - a prior session's claim, not a mechanism.
# SUPERSEDED, kept because a reader who saw it needs to know it was withdrawn: this header used
# to say the index is "APPROXIMATELY the call id", off by one at 0x048C/0x048D, with at least one
# discontinuity whose location is unknown (question I-6).
# THE INDEX IS THE CALL ID, EXACTLY. I-6 was CLOSED 2026-09-07: `record N = verb N` holds across
# all 1,496 family-0 records, on 645 independent anchors agreeing at 89.1% against a 55.7%
# shifted baseline, and a second oppositely-biased metric giving 97.2% against 59.0%. The
# 0x048C/0x048D "off by one" was a column confusion - 003462D0 is begin(0x048D) in that record's
# This correction reached the register on 2026-09-07 and this file on 2026-09-14, because no gate
# reads side-file headers: every stale-prose instrument walks `.md` only. 1,355 authored `#`
# header lines across 211 side files are outside their reach (OPUS, FINAL-AUDIT pass 25).
# FABLE's warning was right and is now resolved. The two trailing columns had been extracted in the OLD
# record frame (records at 01EED720) and therefore named call id n+1's pointers on every row that had
# them. Reproduced before fixing: 147 rows carried a pair, 2 matched (begin, poll)(n), 146 matched
# Both columns are now read for each row's OWN call id, directly from the accessor frame:
#                     control still holds: 1,224 of 1,224 rows agree.
# The column formerly called `poll_handler` is now `begin_handler` and the one called
# `result_handler` is now `poll_handler`; the OLD NAMES WERE BOTH WRONG, not merely shifted - the
# record's fourth slot is the result and it is what `handler` has always held.
# Slot census over all 1,496 records, unchanged by this edit and stated so the frame is checkable:
# begin 277 non-null, poll 230, UNUSED 0, result 1,234. An always-empty THIRD slot is what the
# accessors predict - nothing reads tbl + 0x20n + 0x18 - and it is how the frame was settled.
# WHAT THIS FILE STILL DOES NOT LIST: it has a row per call id that HAS A RESULT CALLBACK, so 259 of
# the 304 asynchronous call ids have no row at all - `wait`, `move` and `turn` among them. See
# members/async-verbs-by-accessor.tsv (FABLE). Adding them is a separate change and is not made here.
# EXTENDED 2026-09-08 with the record's other two handler slots. 261 further mappings were sitting
# unread in a file this database had just adopted.
# ~~The dispatch record is 32 bytes and holds up to three code pointers - begin (+0x00),
# poll (+0x08), result (+0x10).~~ SUPERSEDED 2026-09-19 (OPUS): that is the old record frame and
# it is what put the two trailing columns one call id early. The record is begin +0x00, poll
# +0x08, UNUSED +0x10, result +0x18, based at tbl+8 = 01EED708 - settled by the accessors and by
# the slot census above, where the THIRD slot is empty in all 1,496 records.
# The two counts this block recorded - "poll (+0x08): 122 non-null of 1,224" and "result (+0x10):
# 139 non-null of 1,224" - were counted over the 1,224 rows in the OLD frame and are left here
# only as the record of what was imported. The frame-correct figures are the slot census above.
# The two that are neither are BOTH on call id 05D7, the last record in the extent, and both hold
# FFFFFFFF. They are written as SENTINEL rather than dropped.
# EXTENDED 2026-09-19 (OPUS) with the 259 asynchronous call ids that had no row.
# THE FILE'S SCOPE CHANGED AND THIS IS THE STATEMENT OF IT. It previously held a row per call id that
# has a RESULT callback, which is why a file calling itself the verb-to-handler mapping did not contain
# `wait`, `move` or `turn`. It now also holds every call id that has a BEGIN or a POLL, from
# CONTROL BEFORE MERGING, on the 45 ids the two files already shared: the names agree on 45 of 45,
# and after the re-frame above the begin/poll values agree with ZERO disagreements. That is the
# cross-check that made the merge safe, and it validates the re-frame from a second direction.
# WHAT THE NEW ROWS DO NOT CARRY: `args` is blank on all 259 - the argument counts came from a source
# that only covered the result-callback ids and nothing here establishes them - and `owner` is blank.
# A blank `args` on a new row means UNKNOWN, not zero. ALL 259 have no result callback at all - that
# is precisely why they were absent, since the old scope was "ids with a result" - so `handler` and
# `handler_name` are empty on every one of them by construction rather than by omission.
# (An earlier draft of this note said "224 of the 259". That number was written before it was
# measured; the measurement is 259 of 259 and it is the one that belongs here.)
# PROVENANCE OF THE NAMES, stated because it is not this file's own: `verb` on the new rows is
# `authored_name` from FABLE's census, which does not record where the names came from beyond calling
# them the bundled community catalogue. They agree with this file's own `verb` column on all 45
# shared ids, which is a strong check and is not a provenance.
# The ten family-0 ids the authored catalogue does not name at all (AO-5 / BQ-3) now have rows:
# 1,224 result rows were joined through the catalogue and these ten have no catalogue entry.
# Every slot re-read from the image (01EED700+8+0x20*call_id): begin = poll = +0x10 = 0 in all
# ten, +0x18 non-null - they are RESULT-ONLY records. `verb` is deliberately blank on all ten:
# the catalogue names nothing here and no semantic name is invented; `args` is blank = unknown,
# not zero. 05B2 and 05B3 share result 0050C7F0 - the same alias shape the unnamed pairs carry.
# For completeness: the only other ids with no row are 0330, 0356 and 03B0, whose records are
# all-zero - no handler of any kind, so absence is correct.
